To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the user-centred design of virtual environment applications requires a different approach than that used for traditional software development, (2) the use of a prototyping approach, with the ability to rapidly develop and test prototypes, is an important part of the design process, (3) a user-centred approach is essential in the design and implementation phase of virtual environment development, and (4) the use of virtual environment toolkits can support the development process, but their use should be carefully managed

(1) the user-centred design of virtual environments is a difficult process, (2) the use of a user-centred design process can lead to better virtual environments, but (3) there are many problems in the design of a user-centre design process for VE development, and (4) there are a variety of tools and methods that can be used in the design of virtual environments, and (5) the use of these tools and methods in the design of VE can be facilitated

(1) the design process is iterative and exploratory; (2) the design process involves the user and is user centred; (3) the design process uses prototyping to support exploration of the user interface and the user experience; (4) the design process makes extensive use of a toolkit to support prototyping; (5) the design process supports the use of a toolkit for the implementation of the final system. 1
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation techniques that are required to support the development of virtual environment applications.

understanding how virtual environments can be designed to meet the needs of a particular application domain, and how this technology can then be implemented to meet the needs and requirements of the application.
developing techniques to support the design of interactive systems that are able to adapt to changes in the user’s requirements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
user centred design is the only viable way to design a system, whether it is a virtual environment or any other type of interactive system.
there is no single best way to develop virtual environments.
user-centred design is an important part of the development process for virtual environments and that the development process is iterative and exploratory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the user centred approach is not the only approach to take, but is an approach that should be taken in the design and development of virtual environments.

we are attempting to develop an approach for designing and implementing virtual environments that is user centred, i.e. that focuses on the users’ goals and tasks, and that supports a process of rapid development and prototyping.
virtual environments are not a panacea for all human computer interaction problems and that there are many issues that need to be addressed in their use and development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the user should be involved as early as possible in the development process.
the design of the user interface should be driven by the user, not by the technology.
the design and implementation process for virtual environments is not significantly different from the design and implementation processes for other interactive systems.
